summary: npm marks @antv/x6-plugin-clipboard deprecated and its latest version, 3.0.0, has not changed since 2022-11-25, so it fails the requirement's 12-month maintenance constraint and is capped at avoid despite a clean licence, zero runtime dependencies and no recorded advisories.
reasoning: The registry facts record the package as deprecated ("this package has been deprecated"), which is an upstream signal that it is no longer a supported target for the legacy graph editor.

The latest version is 3.0.0, published 2022-11-25 — roughly four years before this review — so the requirement constraint "Actively maintained (release within 12 months)" is not met; this is the maintenance hard failure that caps the verdict.

The dossier also shows last_publish 2026-09-21 while latest_version remains 3.0.0 from 2022-11-25; that newer publish is not reflected in the latest tag, so it should be checked against the registry before anyone assumes a maintained release exists.

Repository activity does not rescue the package: antvis/x6 was pushed on 2026-10-23 and is not archived (6,751 stars, 1895 forks, 156 open issues), but that activity is monorepo-wide and the plugin itself is deprecated.
Licence and supply-chain hygiene are otherwise clean: MIT in the registry and in the repository, a single 2 KB unpacked artifact, zero runtime dependencies and an empty install-script list.

The dossier records no known advisories for 3.0.0 (the vulnerabilities array is empty), but no advisory scan detail is included, so this is an absence of recorded findings rather than a positive security review.

npm_provenance is false and the provenance note says no attestation was found; the requirement permits that only if exact versions are pinned and the gap is recorded, which adds manual handling to every install.

Fit is conditional: the only peer dependency is @antv/x6 ^3.x, and the dossier does not record whether the legacy application runs X6 v2 or v3 or what its browser baseline is, so compatibility and behaviour preservation are unproven.

No replacement candidate is evidenced here — the request names D3, but the dossier contains no facts about D3 or any other clipboard-capable plugin — so this review rejects the package without naming a specific substitute.
caveats: A deprecated package can be unpublished or frozen by the registry owner at any time, which would break reproducible installs of the legacy application.
There is no npm attestation, so the tarball must be pinned to 3.0.0 and its integrity hash recorded per the requirement's provenance exception.
The peer dependency is @antv/x6 ^3.x; if the legacy application is pinned to X6 v2, this version is not installable without also upgrading the core editor.

Clipboard behaviour that the legacy app may rely on — copy/cut/paste of nodes and edges and its interaction with selection and history — is not verified in the dossier and needs a regression pass before any change.
The 156 open issues and the monorepo release process mean plugin-level fixes are not guaranteed even though the repository itself is active.
Install size was not measured; 2 KB unpacked describes the package artifact, not the cost inside the legacy bundle.
The apparent 2026-09-21 publish date is not attached to the latest version in the dossier and is unverified.

evidence.label: Licence
evidence.detail: MIT in both the npm registry metadata and the antvis/x6 repository metadata, which satisfies the permissive-licence constraint.

evidence.label: Known advisories
evidence.detail: The dossier records an empty vulnerabilities list for 3.0.0, so no advisory is known; the dossier does not include advisory-scan scope, so this is not proof of absence.

evidence.label: npm provenance
evidence.detail: npm_provenance is false and the dossier's provenance note states no npm attestation was found for these facts.

evidence.label: CI publish pipeline
evidence.detail: The dossier contains no publish-workflow evidence for this package; only the registry tarball URL is recorded, so CI publishing could not be confirmed or ruled out.

evidence.label: Maintenance
evidence.detail: Package is marked deprecated; latest version 3.0.0 was published 2022-11-25, far outside the 12-month release window, although the parent repository was pushed 2026-10-23 with 156 open issues.

evidence.label: Dependency footprint
evidence.detail: Zero runtime dependencies, one 2 KB unpacked artifact, no install scripts, and a single peer dependency of @antv/x6 ^3.x; install size was not measured.

evidence.label: TypeScript types
evidence.detail: The registry facts record bundled type declarations and dual module formats for 3.0.0.

evidence.label: Fit with the legacy graph editor
evidence.detail: The dossier records no legacy browser/runtime baseline and no test of clipboard, selection or history behaviour, so behavioural preservation for req-legacy-graph is unmeasured; only the @antv/x6 ^3.x peer range ties it to the existing suite.
